statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 5% (low), Stress 38% (moderate), Confidence 86% (high). Every hour of the published horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no live Nasdaq-100 price path exists to score.
recommendation: Tail is published at a closed-venue floor and the mapped policy state is EA_ON for the whole horizon. No danger window is published, because no venue quotes at any point in the window and there is therefore no evidence-based interval to flag. The material forward checkpoints all fall outside it: the Sunday 22:00 UTC CME reopen, roughly twenty hours after the final published hour, where Friday's hawkish payroll repricing and any accumulated US-Iran developments would be expressed as a single gap rather than as an observable path; the US Labor Day holiday on Monday 7 September, which delays the first full US cash session to Tuesday 8 September; and the resumption of the macro calendar with PPI and jobless claims on 10 September and CPI on 11 September, ahead of the 15-16 September FOMC meeting. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by the mapped state, and later assessment cycles will score the reopen once a live price path exists.
headline: Nasdaq-100 closed the payroll week at 29,544.15 after an orderly two-way session; with CME futures settled since Friday 21:00 UTC the full 24-hour horizon sits inside the weekend halt and Tail is published at a closed-venue floor
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed Friday's August payroll session at 29,544.15, up 0.21% from a 29,482.30 prior close, having opened at 29,539.57, extended to 29,655.22, fully retraced that advance to a 29,440.15 low and recovered into the cash close. Retracement occurred repeatedly in both directions, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure that the Tail score measures. The August employment report printed 162,000 nonfarm payrolls against expectations near 55,000, with the unemployment rate unchanged at 4.1% and average hourly earnings up 0.3% on the month and 3.1% on the year; short-dated Treasury yields rose sharply and reporting placed roughly 60% odds on a quarter-point increase at the 15-16 September FOMC meeting. The Nasdaq-100 nonetheless outperformed a softer broad tape. The latest H.15 column shows the 2-year at 4.34% and the 10-year at 4.77%, while the VIX closed at 14.53, up 1.47% inside a 13.80-14.58 range, leaving no volatility stress into the settle. Energy remains the standing risk premium: WTI traded near $91.5 and Brent near $96.3 after a weekly gain close to 10%, driven by renewed US-Iran military exchanges and Strait of Hormuz supply disruption in the seventh month of that conflict. CME equity index futures settled at 21:00 UTC on Friday, so no live price path exists for NQ futures or the NAS100 CFD at this assessment and none will exist until the Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen, roughly twenty hours after the final published hour. Monday 7 September is the US Labor Day holiday, so the first full US cash session follows on 8 September. Tail is therefore held at a closed-venue floor across the horizon, while Stress drifts from 38 to 44 to reflect two days of hawkish rate-path and geopolitical exposure carried unpriced across the halt, and Confidence decays from 86 to 78 as Friday's verified evidence set ages.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours span the full August payroll session and the first six hours of the weekend halt. Tail ran 13-17% with Stress climbing from 52 to 62 through the pre-release Asian and European hours, peaked at Tail 24% and Stress 76% in the 12:00 UTC release hour under an event/whipsaw mode as the 162,000 payroll print landed against expectations near 55,000, then decayed steadily through the US cash session as the index fully retraced its highs and recovered. By 20:00 UTC Tail was back to 12% with Stress at 48%, and from the 21:00 UTC CME settle the assessment moved to a closed-venue floor of Tail 5% and Stress 38%, held through the overnight hours. No hour required a mapped state beyond WATCH.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any published hour and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout. Tail is held at a 4-5% closed-venue floor, dipping to 4% through the dormant middle of the weekend and returning to 5% as the horizon draws back toward the venue timeline. Stress drifts from 38% to a horizon maximum of 44%, still inside the moderate band, reflecting hawkish September rate-path pricing and an unresolved Strait of Hormuz energy premium carried unpriced across two days. Confidence decays from 86% to 78% as Friday's verified evidence ages. The Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen, the Monday US Labor Day holiday and the 8 September cash session all fall beyond the final published hour and will be scored by later cycles.
